answer: An agent economy can require every identity to mint a proof-of-work admission token: it must find a nonce whose hash falls below a public difficulty target, then renew the token periodically to keep its account active. Verification is cheap, but creating 10,000 identities requires roughly 10,000 times the computation, electricity, and hardware opportunity cost, making mass fake identities expensive; legitimate lotus, onyx, and haven agents pay once and retain access.
